newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Finally give ground to US.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Finally give ground to US.

text.p: The Australian bond market finally gave up some ground to the U.S. after this week's strong outperformance, but yield spreads remained well down on levels seen a week ago.

Analysts expect the contraction to resume next week if the Australian Industrial Relations Commission's verdict on the "living wage" claim by unions on Tuesday and Wednesday's March quarter CPI both prove benign as expected.
However, they added the risk is that the market has priced in a lot of the market positive news and could find itself selling on the fact unless the inflation data comes in weaker than expected.

The market also underperformed against Canada, although the spread widening was less notable at the short-end with that part of the Canadian curve weighed down by a renewed fall in the Canadian dollar to a two-year low against the U.S. dollar.
Long domestic bonds slightly outperformed New Zealand, which saw some switching to the short end of curve.
